name: bluewater-21-every-business-is-a-boat
lines: Every business is a boat.
And almost every owner is sailing it alone.
Let me show you what that looks like. Then I'll show you the crew you're missing.
This is Sam. Made up, like everyone in this story. Sam runs a tree service.
Eleven years ago, Sam left the harbor. One truck. One customer. No map.
Out here, Sam does every job on the boat.
Sam steers. That's the work itself. And Sam is very good at steering.
But a boat needs more than a captain.
The six jobs.
Job one. The lookout. Somebody has to watch for customers on the horizon.
That's being found. Your listing. Your website. The search at nine p.m., when a tree comes down on someone's fence.
Sam's lookout post is empty. It has been for years.
Job two. The signal lamp. It tells other ships you exist.
That's your ads and your content. The light only reaches as far as someone keeps it lit.
Sam lights it every few months. Then a busy week comes, and it goes dark.
Job three. The radio. When someone calls the boat, someone answers.
Sam is up a tree with a chainsaw. The radio rings out.
Job four. The logbook. Every customer, every quote, every promise, written down.
Sam's logbook is a text thread and a good memory. The good memory is getting tired.
Job five. The flag. It's how people know whose boat this is.
That's your name, your trucks, your reviews. What people say after you've sailed away.
Job six. The navigator. Somebody who looks at the numbers and says, we're drifting.
Sam has never once had time to look at the numbers.
The storm.
For years, it works anyway. Calm water. Referrals drift in.
Then one winter, the calls slow down. And nobody knows why.
No lookout saw it coming. No log to check. No light on.
Sam does what every owner does. Works harder. Steers harder.
But you can't steer your way out of an empty lookout post.
The crew.
Here's the part nobody says out loud.
Sam isn't bad at marketing. Sam is one person doing seven jobs.
The fix was never a new trick. It was a crew.
A lookout, so you're found. A lamp that stays lit. A radio that gets answered.
A logbook nobody has to remember. A flag people recognize. A navigator who tells you the truth.
And a captain, who gets to do the one job only they can do.
The honest part. A crew doesn't change the weather.
Some months are slow. No one can promise you calm seas, or how many calls come in.
What a crew changes is this. You stop finding out last.
Sam's story is made up. So Sam gets a second ending.
Spring. Same boat. Same captain. Six posts filled.
A stranger searches at nine p.m. This time, Sam's light is on.
That's all a marketing department is. The rest of your crew.
Your business. Our marketing department. Bluewater Co dot C A.
